validity.researcher_notes: THREE separate numeric conflicts surfaced against independent sources: (1) SegmentCost: the sheet records $3,500,000,000 (3.5 BILLION USD) with no ref. EIA's Historical Projects workbook states 'Cost (millions): 300' for this exact project -- i.e. $300 million, off by a factor of ~11.7x from the sheet. I could not find any source stating $3.5B for this project (searched the harvested wiki citations, the Pipeline News PDF -- no cost field given there -- and general web/SEC EDGAR full-text search); $3.5B looks like a data-entry error, possibly copied from a much larger unrelated project. Proposing the EIA-sourced $300M as the corrected value (single independent source; a second source stating cost was not found -- FERC's PF15-30 docket, which is blocked to scripted access, is the logical second source and should be checked before finalizing). (2) ShelvedYear=2020 / CancelledYear=2022: both EIA (Last Updated Date 2018-01-24, Status=Cancelled) and Pipeline News (entry revision date 11/17, i.e. Nov 2017, Status='withdrawn its pre-filing application') show the project was ALREADY cancelled/withdrawn by late 2017/early 2018 -- four to five years before the sheet's recorded dates. This looks like GEM's dormancy-inference heuristic (2y->shelved, 4y->cancelled) applied from a stale 'last touched' date rather than the actual withdrawal date, now contradicted by hard primary evidence. I'm proposing CancelledYear=2017 as the best-evidenced estimate (last date before which cancellation was already recorded); I could not pin an exact month/day, and recommend checking FERC docket PF15-30 (elibrary.ferc.gov, JS-only interface, not fetchable by curl/WebFetch from this session) for the precise withdrawal order date. I found no evidence of a distinct intervening 'shelved' phase separate from the cancellation itself (a FERC pre-filing withdrawal is typically a single step), so I'm not proposing a replacement ShelvedYear -- flagging that the field may not belong on this row at all, for a human to decide. See the companion status_reviews record for the ShelvedCancelledType=inferred->confirmed change this evidence supports. (3) EndState/Province: the sheet (and Pipeline News, which names 'Bryan County, OK - Lamar County, TX' matching the sheet exactly) both put the pipeline crossing into Texas. But EIA's workbook row for this same project lists Beg_State=OK, End_State=OK, and explicitly 'Crosses State Border: No' -- i.e. EIA's own tracking treats this as an all-Oklahoma project, not one crossing into Texas. This is a genuine, unresolved conflict between two independent, reputable sources (a government dataset vs. a trade-press directory that otherwise matches the sheet exactly on length and diameter). EIA's own project note ('Very little details on project that proposes similar route to other proposed pipeline projects') suggests EIA itself was working from incomplete information, so I am NOT overriding the sheet/Pipeline-News endpoint with EIA's state flag, but this needs a human check against the actual FERC PF15-30 filing before the endpoint state is treated as fully confirmed -- leaving EndState/Province contested with no candidate replacement (evidence only shows the current value is in dispute, not what the correct value is).
